title: Work & study
goal: Talk about jobs, school and the office, and say what you can, can't, may and must do.
intro:
Bengaluru is India's tech capital, and office Kannada is full of English: ಮೀಟಿಂಗ್, ಡೆಡ್‌ಲೈನ್, ಪ್ರಾಜೆಕ್ಟ್. But the grammar holding those words together is pure Kannada, and the native words are what you'll see in schools, government offices and newspapers.

This unit covers **ability** ('can'), **permission** ('may') and **obligation** ('must, have to'). Notice how many of these use the dative subject again: 'to me, doing it becomes possible'.

vocab.note: f: ಶಿಕ್ಷಕಿ shikṣaki. Pupils say ಮೇಷ್ಟ್ರು / ಟೀಚರ್.
ಅರ್ಥ ಆಗು 'to be understood': ನನಗೆ ಅರ್ಥ ಆಯ್ತು 'I understood'.

vocab.en: to become, happen; to be possible
vocab.note: Past ಆಯಿತು / spoken ಆಯ್ತು; negative ಆಗಲ್ಲ 'can't be done'.

phrases.en: My mother teaches at a school.

phrases.native: ನನಗೆ ಅರ್ಥ ಆಗಲಿಲ್ಲ, ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಸಲ ಹೇಳ್ತೀರಾ?
phrases.roman: nanage artha āgalilla, innondu sala hēḷtīrā?

phrases.en: I can read Kannada, but I can't write it.
I have an exam tomorrow, I have to study.

grammar.title: Ability and permission: 'can', 'know how to', 'may'
grammar.body:
**Can (be able to)**: infinitive + **ಆಗು**, with the person in the **dative**. Written infinitive is **-ಅಲು** (ಮಾಡಲು); spoken is **-ಓಕೆ** (ಮಾಡೋಕೆ) or Bengaluru **-ಅಕ್ಕೆ** (ಮಾಡಕ್ಕೆ):
• ನನಗೆ ಬರೋಕೆ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ 'I can come' (lit. to me, to come becomes possible)
• ನನಗೆ ಬರೋಕೆ ಆಗಲ್ಲ 'I can't come'
• ನಿಮಗೆ ನಾಳೆ ಬರೋಕೆ ಆಗುತ್ತಾ? 'Can you come tomorrow?'
• Past: ಬರೋಕೆ ಆಗಲಿಲ್ಲ 'couldn't come'

**Know how to (skill)**: infinitive + **ಬರು** 'come': ನನಗೆ ಈಜೋಕೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ 'I can swim', ಅವನಿಗೆ ಡ್ರೈವ್ ಮಾಡೋಕೆ ಬರಲ್ಲ 'he can't drive'. (Same as knowing a language: ನನಗೆ ಕನ್ನಡ ಬರುತ್ತೆ.)

**May / it's allowed / might**: infinitive + **-ಬಹುದು**: ನೀವು ಹೋಗಬಹುದು 'you may go', ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಫೋಟೋ ತೆಗೆಯಬಹುದಾ? 'can I take photos here?'. Negative: **-ಬಾರದು** 'mustn't'.

Literary Kannada also has -ಬಲ್ಲೆ 'I can' (ಮಾಡಬಲ್ಲೆ), which you'll see in writing.

examples.en: You mustn't use your phone in class.

grammar.title: Obligation: must, have to, had to, should have
grammar.body:
You met **infinitive + -ಬೇಕು** 'must, have to' in unit 9. It has several useful variants:
• **-ಬೇಕು** 'have to / should': ನಾನು ಓದಬೇಕು 'I have to study'
• **-ಲೇಬೇಕು** 'absolutely must' (emphatic -ಏ): ಹೋಗಲೇಬೇಕು 'I simply must go'
• **-ಬೇಕಾಗುತ್ತೆ** 'will have to': ನಾಳೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಬೇಕಾಗುತ್ತೆ 'I'll have to work tomorrow'
• **-ಬೇಕಾಯ್ತು** 'had to': ಶನಿವಾರ ಆಫೀಸಿಗೆ ಹೋಗಬೇಕಾಯ್ತು 'I had to go to the office on Saturday'
• **-ಬೇಕಿತ್ತು** 'should have / was supposed to': ಬೇಗ ಬರಬೇಕಿತ್ತು 'you should have come early'
• **-ಬೇಕಾಗಿಲ್ಲ** 'don't have to'

None of these change for person: the subject can be in the nominative (ನಾನು) or, with -ಬೇಕಾಗುತ್ತೆ / -ಬೇಕಾಯ್ತು, often the dative (ನನಗೆ).

examples.en: We have to arrive before ten.
This project absolutely must be finished today.

examples.native: ನಿನ್ನೆ ರಾತ್ರಿ ತುಂಬಾ ಹೊತ್ತು ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಬೇಕಾಯ್ತು
examples.roman: ninne rātri tumbā hottu kelasa māḍabēkāytu
examples.en: I had to work late last night.
You should have told me earlier.
No need to go to school tomorrow, it's a holiday.

dialogue.title: A new job
dialogue.setting: Rahul meets his old college friend Pooja at a café and catches up on work.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.en: Hey Rahul, how's the new job?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದೆ, ಆದ್ರೆ ತುಂಬಾ ಕೆಲಸ. ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ಹತ್ತು ಗಂಟೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಬೇಕು.
lines.roman: chennāgide, ādre tumbā kelasa. pratidina hattu gaṇṭe kelasa māḍabēku.
lines.en: It's good, but lots of work. I have to work ten hours every day.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.en: Oh no! Can't you work from home?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ವಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಎರಡು ದಿನ ಮಾಡಬಹುದು. ನಿನ್ನ ಕೆಲಸ ಹೇಗಿದೆ?
lines.roman: vārakke eraḍu dina māḍabahudu. ninna kelasa hēgide?
lines.en: I can, two days a week. How's your work?

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: ನಾನು ಈಗ ಮಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆ ಗಣಿತ ಕಲಿಸ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ. ಮುಂದಿನ ವಾರ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಇದೆ.
lines.roman: nānu īga makkaḷige gaṇita kalistiddīni. mundina vāra parīkṣe ide.
lines.en: I'm teaching maths to kids now. There are exams next week.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ಓಹ್, ನೀನು ಟೀಚರ್ ಆದೆಯಾ! ಮಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆ ಅರ್ಥ ಆಗುತ್ತಾ?
lines.roman: ōh, nīnu ṭīchar ādeyā! makkaḷige artha āguttā?
lines.en: Oh, you became a teacher! Do the kids understand?

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: ಕೆಲವರಿಗೆ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ, ಕೆಲವರಿಗೆ ಆಗಲ್ಲ. ಪ್ರಯತ್ನ ಮಾಡ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ!
lines.roman: kelavarige āgutte, kelavarige āgalla. prayatna māḍtiddīni!
lines.en: Some do, some don't. I'm trying!

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ಸರಿ, ನಾನು ಈಗ ಹೋಗಲೇಬೇಕು. ಮೂರು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಮೀಟಿಂಗ್ ಇದೆ.
lines.roman: sari, nānu īga hōgalēbēku. mūru gaṇṭege mīṭiṅg ide.
lines.en: Okay, I really must go now. I have a meeting at three.

culture: Teachers are traditionally shown great respect: students call male teachers ಮೇಷ್ಟ್ರು or ಸಾರ್ and female teachers ಮೇಡಂ or ಟೀಚರ್. Kannada is compulsory in Karnataka state schools, and there is active debate about Kannada-medium vs English-medium education. The informal particle -ಓ (ಏನೋ, ಬಾರೋ) is used to address a male friend, and -ಏ (ಏನೇ, ಬಾರೇ) to address a female friend (Pooja's ಏನೋ to Rahul above). Use them only with close friends: with anyone else they sound rude.

He's a lawyer. (respectful)
My younger brother is a teacher.

sentences.roman: namma mēṣṭru tumbā chennāgi pāṭha māḍtāre.
sentences.en: Our teacher teaches really well.
Today's lesson is very easy.
She teaches English at a college.
Will you teach me Kannada?

lessons.title: Can you? May I?

tip.title: Can, know how to, may
tip.body:
- **Able to**: person + **-ಗೆ**, verb + **-ಓಕೆ**, then **ಆಗು**: ನನಗೆ **ಬರೋಕೆ** ಆಗುತ್ತೆ 'I can come', ಆಗಲ್ಲ 'I can't'.
- **Know how to** (a skill): -ಓಕೆ + **ಬರು**: ನನಗೆ ಓದೋಕೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ 'I can read'.
- **May / allowed**: **-ಬಹುದು**: ಹೋಗಬಹುದಾ? 'may I go?'; not allowed: **-ಬಾರದು**.

new: ನನಗೆ ಕನ್ನಡ ಓದೋಕೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ, ಬರೆಯೋಕೆ ಬರಲ್ಲ

sentences.en: Can you come on Saturday?
Sorry, Saturday doesn't work for me.
He can drive a car.
Can you speak Kannada?
A little bit.
I can't finish all the work today.
May I go home now?
Yes, you may go.
You mustn't talk in class.

sentences.native: ಇದು ನನಗೆ ಸಾಧ್ಯ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಆದ್ರೆ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ.
sentences.roman: idu nanage sādhya illa, ādre prayatna māḍtīni.
sentences.en: This isn't possible for me, but I'll try.

lessons.title: Questions and answers
new: ನನಗೆ ಅರ್ಥ ಆಗಲಿಲ್ಲ, ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಸಲ ಹೇಳ್ತೀರಾ?

What's the answer to this question?
Your answer is right.
Write answers to all the questions.
What does this mean?
I get it now, thank you.
When is the exam?
The exam was really hard.

lessons.title: Have to, had to, should have

tip.title: Must, had to, should have
tip.body:
- **-ಬೇಕು** 'have to': ಹೋಗಬೇಕು. Emphatic **-ಲೇಬೇಕು** 'simply must': ಹೋಗಲೇಬೇಕು.
- **-ಬೇಕಾಗುತ್ತೆ** 'will have to', **-ಬೇಕಾಯ್ತು** 'had to', **-ಬೇಕಿತ್ತು** 'should have'.
- **-ಬೇಕಾಗಿಲ್ಲ** 'don't have to'.
- None of them change for the person: ನಾನು / ನೀವು / ಅವರು ಹೋಗಬೇಕು.

sentences.en: I have to go to a meeting at ten.

sentences.native: ನಿನ್ನೆ ರಾತ್ರಿ ಹತ್ತು ಗಂಟೆವರೆಗೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಬೇಕಾಯ್ತು.
sentences.roman: ninne rātri hattu gaṇṭevarege kelasa māḍabēkāytu.
sentences.en: Yesterday I had to work until ten at night.
I'll have to talk to the manager tomorrow.
You should have come to the meeting.
You don't have to come to the office on Saturday.
I simply must go to Mysuru tomorrow.
I have to call the manager.
When does the salary come in?
My colleagues are really nice people.
